note: Verified against legislation.nsw.gov.au on 2026-08-14. Interpretation Act 1987 s 36 is disapplied to the UCPR by r 1.11(5), so UCPR period rules rely on r 1.11 alone. UCPR rollover turns on days the registry is closed (r 1.11(4)); the script approximates registry-closed days with the weekend-and-public-holiday table, and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the registry was open. An entry returned to pending-verification fails closed until re-verified.

computation_provisions.summary: Reckoning of time: a period dating from a day, act or event excludes that day (s 36(1)); where the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public or bank holiday in the place where the thing is to be done, it may be done on the first following day that is not such a day (s 36(2)); extension powers survive expiry (s 36(3)). Disapplied to the UCPR by UCPR r 1.11(5) — use for other NSW instruments only.

computation_provisions.summary: Any period fixed by the rules, a judgment, an order or a document is reckoned excluding the trigger day (r 1.11(2)); for periods of 5 days or less, registry-closed days are excluded (r 1.11(3)); if the last day falls on a day the registry is closed, the thing may be done on the next day the registry is open (r 1.11(4)); Interpretation Act 1987 s 36 does not apply (r 1.11(5)). Extension and abridgment sit in r 1.12.

period_rules.label: Defence after service of statement of claim
period_rules.trigger: Service of the statement of claim on the defendant
warnings: The rule is subject to any other time the court directs (r 14.3(1)) and to r 14.3(2) where a summary judgment motion intervenes.
Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a NSW public holiday; r 1.11(4) turns on days the registry is closed — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.

period_rules.label: Notice of appeal to the Court of Appeal (no leave required, no notice of intention filed)
period_rules.trigger: Material date as defined in r 51.2 (for a Supreme Court judgment, the date it is given; for an order, the date it is made)
warnings: This 28-day period applies only where leave is not required and no notice of intention to appeal has been filed; if a notice of intention was filed r 51.9 governs, and an appeal pursuant to leave must be filed within 7 days after leave (r 51.16(1)(a)).
Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a NSW public holiday; r 1.11(4) turns on days the registry is closed — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.
